**NOTE:** Folders in **boldface** denote playable characters.

Fontaine
--------

![Image 1: Characters in Genshin Impact: Fontaine](https://static.tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pub/images/emblem_fontaine.png)

**Fontaine** is the nation of Water and Justice, located on the top of a submarine plateau in the middle of an inland sea in central Teyvat and under the patronage of the Hydro Archon, Focalors.

While nominally ruled by Focalors, much of Fontaine's day-to-day governance is administered by a system of courts led by the Iudex (Chief Justice) Neuvillette. In addition, Fontaine is also renowned as one of the most technologically advanced nations in Teyvat, being the birthplace of such marvels as Kameras, firearms, and autonomous machines called Meks, as well as a major center of fashion.

open/close all folders

* * *

General Tropes

*   [Absurdly Spacious Sewer](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/AbsurdlySpaciousSewer "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/AbsurdlySpaciousSewer"): According to Julien (and as seen during the teaser for Fontaine), the sewerage system of Fontaine is huge enough to traverse through. It is also big enough to house the lower-class citizens as the Fleuve Cendre district.
*   [Alternate Techline](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/AlternateTechline "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/AlternateTechline"): Fontaine is one of the most tech-savvy nations, second only to Snezhnaya, and many technologies that have appeared in other nations, such as the well-known Kamera and its variant, the Film Kamera, originated from Fontaine. It also features other impressive bits of technology, such as Clockwork Meka, which protects Fontaine, firearms, and Aquabuses, which serve as the region's main method of transportation.
*   [At the Opera Tonight](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/AtTheOperaTonight "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/AtTheOperaTonight"): Rather than a traditional courthouse, court operations and trials are presided in Opera Epiclese on Erinnyes Island. This makes Dainsleif's remarks about how Fontaine's Archon "lives for the **spectacle** of the courtroom" rather ominous.
*   [Artificial Human](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ArtificialHuman "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ArtificialHuman"): Every last Fontainian is initially not a true human, but Oceanids given pseudo-human mimic forms by Egeria, the previous Hydro Archon, using a piece of the power of the Primordial Sea, from which all life in Teyvat was born. These mimics would go on to birth more mimics with their piece of the Primordial Sea's power and eventually live out their mortal lives, until the people's true nature as Oceanids was lost to the generations, which is [lampshaded](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/LampshadeHanging "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/LampshadeHanging") by the Chinese localization calling the Hydro Tulpa, an aggregate of Hydro Mimics, a “Hydro Mimic Human.” This is also why only Fontainians dissolve in the Primordial Seawaters: if too much of the Primordial Sea's power fills them, their mimic forms pop like a balloon, causing all the Primordial Sea's power to escape them, killing the human and turning them back into an Oceanid.

*   [Divine Punishment](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/DivinePunishment "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/DivinePunishment"): [The Great Flood](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/TheGreatFlood "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/TheGreatFlood") that threatens Fontaine in [The Prophecy](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/TheProphecy "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/TheProphecy") is Celestia's punishment for Egeria's sin of appropriating the power of the Primordial Sea to create human mimics out of her Oceanid [familiars](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/Familiars "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/Familiars").

In the next two acts, the Traveler discovers the involvement of the All-Devouring Narwhal as the threat of [The Great Flood](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/TheGreatFlood "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/TheGreatFlood") looms larger, placing greater pressure on Furina, whose nervous and evasive behavior made it clear that she has a [Plot-Driving Secret](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/PlotDrivingSecret "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/PlotDrivingSecret"). *   [Event Title](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/EventTitle "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/EventTitle"): Fontaine's related Archon Quest, as well as its fifth act, is titled "Masquerade of The Guilty"note , and indeed the Traveler meets numerous people (an entire nation, as it turns out) pretending to be something they are not.
*   [Everyone Has Standards](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/EveryoneHasStandards "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/EveryoneHasStandards"): While the people of Fontaine are usually glad when a criminal is convicted for their crime and are disgusted at Furina when they learn that she isn't the real Hydro Archon, everyone present in the trial is horrified when the Oratrice seemingly sentences her to death.
*   [Fairytale Motifs](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/FairytaleMotifs "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/FairytaleMotifs"): The origin of the entire native population of Fontaine is loosely based on _[The Little Mermaid](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Literature/TheLittleMermaid "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Literature/TheLittleMermaid")_. Long ago, their ancestors were [Oceanids](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/OurNymphsAreDifferent "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/OurNymphsAreDifferent") who admired the beauty and romanticism of the humans they saw on land, and Egeria granted their wish to be human-like by appropriating the power of the Primordial Sea, with the caveat that their artificial humanity can be destroyed by contact with Primordial Seawater, forcing them to dissolve and return to water. Over the millennia, this secret was forgotten by later generations and only rediscovered on the cusp of a looming [Divine Punishment](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/DivinePunishment "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/DivinePunishment") by Celestia in the form of [The Great Flood](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/TheGreatFlood "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/TheGreatFlood"). However, Focalors, the current Hydro Archon and last of the Oceanid pseudo-humans, cared more about the continuation of her subjects' existence than her immortal life, and thus successfully planned and executed a centuries-long scheme to make the [Heroic Sacrifice](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/HeroicSacrifice "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/HeroicSacrifice") necessary to turn them into true humans. The title of the play that Furina gets involved in during her Story Quest is even called "The Little Oceanid", which has a similar story based on the life of the director that the play was a tribute to, while Sigewinne's Story Quest presents a more personal take on the tale with the revelation that she ingested a potion to give herself a humanoid appearance, in exchange for her mentor dissolving herself into Primordial Seawater to produce the potion and her being imprisoned in the Fortress of Meropide for violating ancient laws prohibiting transhumanism.

    *   Sinthe is a diluted concoction of Primordial Seawater that induces feelings of euphoria and pleasant hallucinations, but harms one's mental faculties with long-term consumption. By the time of the Fontaine Archon Quest, Sinthe addiction has already destroyed many families, and Navia seeks to end the operation in her deceased father's place.
    *   The solution derived from dissolved Fontainians can be used as an active ingredient in a face-swapping lotion as well as a potion to reshape Melusines' features into humanoid limbs and skin.

*   [Girls with Guns](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/GirlsWithGuns "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/GirlsWithGuns"): Fontaine, being a nation of technology, features several female characters who use various guns: Sigewinne (tranquilizer and bubble gun), Navia (parasol rifle and cannons), Chevreuse (musket), and Clorinde (pistol).
*   [Gods Need Prayer Badly](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/GodsNeedPrayerBadly "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/GodsNeedPrayerBadly"): Taken a step further than in previous nations. Oceanids
--------

A race of mermaid-like creatures once associated with Fontaine and faithful followers of Egeria, the previous Hydro Archon, a vast majority of which have since chosen exile following the death of said Archon and their refusal to acknowledge her successor, Furina/Focalors.

In General

*   [Animal Motifs](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/AnimalMotifs "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/AnimalMotifs"): The Oceanids' [Shapeshifter Default Form](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ShapeshifterDefaultForm "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ShapeshifterDefaultForm") look similar to [sea angels![Image 10](https://static.tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pub/external_link.gif)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_angel), a type of sea slug with wing-like appendages.
*   [Bizarre Alien Reproduction](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/BizarreAlienReproduction "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/BizarreAlienReproduction"): An ["Ancient Natural History Excerpt"![Image 11](https://static.tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pub/external_link.gif)](https://genshin-impact.fandom.com/wiki/Institute_of_Natural_Philosophy#Ancient_Natural_History_Excerpts) in-game states that Fontaine's researchers can't even find a suitable name for the method in which Oceanids "increase in the number" with the most concise description being, verbatim, "they approach the Hydro Archon or an elder for permission to claim... um, a thing, which results in their division into little Oceanids."
*   [Cyclops](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/Cyclops "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/Cyclops"): In their [Shapeshifter Default Form](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ShapeshifterDefaultForm "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ShapeshifterDefaultForm"), Oceanids have a single white eye in their otherwise featureless face.
*   [Elemental Embodiment](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ElementalEmbodiment "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ElementalEmbodiment"): The Oceanids are composed entirely of Hydro, which is reflected when Elemetal Sight is used.
*   [Familiar](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/Familiar "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/Familiar"): The Oceanids served the previous Hydro Archon Egeria prior to her death, and the current one Focalors was also one before her ascension.
*   [Fusion Dance](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/FusionDance "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/FusionDance"): Multiple Oceanids are able to merge together, Rhodeia is one such example. Lyris was also able to merge with Mary-Ann Guillotin but since Mary-Ann was an Oceanid turned human as all Fontanians were at the time, merging with humans may not reguarly be possible.
*   [Morphic Resonance](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/MorphicResonance "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/MorphicResonance"): Every Oceanid in human form seen so far has had blue hair and blue eyes. Dulphy, an actor in Fontaine, puts on a blue wig (she already had blue eyes) to play an Oceanid on stage so it seems to be common knowledge at least in Fontaine despite no one seeming to know this detail whenever the Traveler has encountered real Oceanids in human form.
*   [Occult Blue Eyes](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/OccultBlueEyes "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/OccultBlueEyes"): Their human forms always have supernaturally glowing blue eyes.
*   [One-Gender Race](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/OneGenderRace "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/OneGenderRace"): The mythological origin of Oceanids describes the creation of the first one, and every single one since, with feminine pronouns. Though the species is very squarely biologically asexual, no complaint has been brought up about the gendering so far.
*   [Our Nymphs Are Different](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/OurNymphsAreDifferent "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/OurNymphsAreDifferent"): The Oceanids, in their [Shapeshifter Default Form](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ShapeshifterDefaultForm "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ShapeshifterDefaultForm"), are single-eyed Hydro-elemental beings whose have wings and tails like fish, and their mood can affect the quality of the water they inhabit.
*   [Religious and Mythological Theme Naming](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ReligiousAndMythologicalThemeNaming "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ReligiousAndMythologicalThemeNaming"): All natural-born, non-pseudo-human Oceanids are named or have similar names as their counterparts in [Greek mythology](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Myth/ClassicalMythology "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Myth/ClassicalMythology").
*   [Self-Imposed Exile](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/SelfImposedExile "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/SelfImposedExile"): Many of the Oceanids are said to have left Fontaine as they did not get along with the current Hydro Archon Focalors. The main reason they fled Fontaine, according to Idyia, is that the water there is now filled with pain and hatred, rendering them unable to survive there and to seek refuge elsewhere. This ends up foreshadowing the existence of the Primordial Sea and the prophecy created by Celestia to flood Fontaine.
*   [Voluntary Shapeshifting](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/VoluntaryShapeshifting "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/VoluntaryShapeshifting"): Seeing how Rhodeia always mentions "the power of water is its ability to take any shape" and Idyia and Callirhoe were able to shift into a human form, Oceanids are most likely able to take on any form they wish, though from Callirhoe's words, it can take significant effort spanning decades for them to accumulate enough power in order to maintain those forms for even a short period of time.
*   [Water Is Blue](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/WaterIsBlue "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/WaterIsBlue"): As Hydro-elemental beings, blue naturally colors every part of the Oceanids' human forms, from their hair, clothing to [Occult Blue Eyes](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/OccultBlueEyes "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/OccultBlueEyes").
*   [Water Is Womanly](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/WaterIsWomanly "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/WaterIsWomanly"): All Oceanids introduced in the game use feminine pronouns. Subverted later in Fontaine, where male Oceanids appear as well, but only because they were pseudo-humans.
*   [What Is This Thing You Call "Love"?](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/WhatIsThisThingYouCallLove "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/WhatIsThisThingYouCallLove"): The combo of immortality and being elemental beings with a wildly different idea of consciousness makes Oceanids naturally struggle to understand the emotions of other creatures, something not at all helping in Egeria's mission for them to comprehend all forms of life. Some, such as Idyia and Callirhoe, have come to understand human emotions enough to even recognize them in themselves while many others asked for Egeria to make them human, leading to the entire native human population of Fontaine.

Melusines
---------

A race of amphibious beings originating from the Elynas region who were introduced to human society four-hundred years ago by Neuvillette.

In General

*   [Adorable Abomination](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/AdorableAbomination "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/AdorableAbomination"): Despite their cute appearances, they are creatures born from the wounds and broken flesh of their "Father" [Elynas](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/EldritchAbomination "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/EldritchAbomination").
*   [The Ageless](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/TheAgeless "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/TheAgeless"): They don't seem to age beyond adulthood and the oldest known living Melusine, Siegwinne, shows no signs of aged frailty. They also seem highly resistant to sickness and injury as well. That said, they can still die from misfortune and Neuvilette's Character Story reveals one of the first Melusine Gardes was [Driven to Suicide](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/DrivenToSuicide "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/DrivenToSuicide").
*   [Always Lawful Good](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/AlwaysLawfulGood "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/AlwaysLawfulGood"): All the Melusines that can be interacted with are universally kind and gentle beings, and accordingly, the majority of Fontainian humans hold them in high esteem. It's noted that any Melusine who commits a crime would have to face the consequences like anyone else, but even then, Sigewinne, the sole Melusine so far to serve a prison sentence, is a rather benign case as her only crime was to [take on a humanoid appearance](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/NoTranshumanismAllowed "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/NoTranshumanismAllowed") to [save a little girl's life.](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ScrewTheRulesImDoingWhatsRight "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ScrewTheRulesImDoingWhatsRight")
*   [Amazing Technicolor Population](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/AmazingTechnicolorPopulation "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/AmazingTechnicolorPopulation"): Melusines have pastel skin colors.
*   [Cartoon Creature](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/CartoonCreature "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/CartoonCreature"): They’re intended to be anthropomorphic sea slugs and were born from a gigantic dragon but they look more like bunny or mouse people.
*   [Cute Monster Girl](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/CuteMonsterGirl "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/CuteMonsterGirl"): They are a race of female-identifying [Ridiculously Cute Critters](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/RidiculouslyCuteCritter "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/RidiculouslyCuteCritter").
*   [Exotic Eye Designs](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ExoticEyeDesigns "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ExoticEyeDesigns"): Some of the Melusines, like Elphane, have white pupils shaped like four windmill blades.
*   [Fantastic Racism](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/FantasticRacism "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/FantasticRacism"): Initially but defied. Back when the Melusines were new to Fontaine, they faced mistreatment and distrust from humans due to their alien appearances, and their association with the equally new Neuvillette. This only got worse when they were quickly inducted into the Marechaussee Phantom, enough that one Melusine _committed suicide_ over it (and for one human, who advocated for their rights, to slaughter the hate group responsible). While it took centuries for Melusines to be integrated into human society, Neuvilette's efforts finally paid off, and most Fontainians now treat them as citizens, intolerant of any discrimination towards them and can be extremely protective of them. Neuvilette even introduced a law [prohibiting Melusines from being referred to with "it/its" pronouns](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ItIsDehumanizing "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ItIsDehumanizing"). Sigewinne's story quest goes a bit more in depth about this, with _both_ Melusines and humans mutually distrusting each other and humans who liked Melusines being shunned. However, this may not be the case for visitors from other nations who are perplexed by the Melusine's existence, with a Sumeru researcher who attempted to treat the Melusine like animals was expelled from the region for his ignorance. Following his expulsion, a message appeared on the Romaritime Harbor Bulletin Board:**Notice to Travelers:** Special reminder: Attention, travelers. "Melusines" are citizens of Fontaine and part of our nation, and not pets or monsters. Please respect the individual rights of Melusines and the customs of their race.

Fontaine Research Institute of Kinetic Energy Engineering
---------------------------------------------------------

A research center located in northwestern Fontaine. Founded by Alain Guillotin four-hundred years ago, it was dedicated to studying machines and energy before being destroyed by a gravity experiment gone wrong in an attempt to create a solution to the prophesied flooding. Its remaining members have worked tirelessly to try and rebuild since then using whatever they can salvage and with support from the government, rebranding as the New Fontaine Research Institute.

In General

*   [Bungling Inventor](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/BunglingInventor "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/BunglingInventor"): Inventions of the Fontaine Research Institute fall squarely into two categories; as impressive as they are dangerous ([Clockwork Meka](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/MechaMooks "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/MechaMooks") and the [Experimental Field Generator](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/GravityMaster "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/GravityMaster")) or safe but of limited value ([Fonta](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/BlandNameProduct "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/BlandNameProduct")). Their reputation is accordingly low.
*   [Does This Remind You of Anything?](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/DoesThisRemindYouOfAnything "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/DoesThisRemindYouOfAnything"): A destroyed facility caused by unstable creations and operator error with mentions of radiation fields being present brings to mind that of the [Chernobyl Disaster](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/UsefulNotes/Chernobyl "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/UsefulNotes/Chernobyl"), albeit on a much smaller and more fantastic scale.
*   [For Science!](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ForScience "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ForScience"): The Institute's first and foremost are experiments and inventions, just because. As noted by Berrypuff's former caretaker, even pointless (not to mention _impractical_) inventions get approved by superiors at the expense of animal care simply because its beneath them, to the point that they might as well "become mechanisms themselves" simply because they're into inventions too much. According to the flavour text for the "Pure Water" and the legend surrounding it, they also have very little if not zero interest in potions and alchemy compared to nations like Mondstadt due to them not taking it seriously as an academic discipline even when a prodigy in that field once existed amongst their ranks. Tellingly, Sigewinne categorizes them as being completely _separate_ from normal humans.**Sigewinne**: Researchers are a very special breed of human.
    
*   [Gameplay and Story Segregation](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/GameplayAndStorySegregation "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/GameplayAndStorySegregation"): There are supposedly radiation fields that were caused by the explosion, yet there is nothing to indicate so such as losing health in certain areas. Zig-zagged in that the researchers have been careful in finding them while rebuilding, but so far have thankfully found none if very few.
*   [Gone Horribly Wrong](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/GoneHorriblyWrong "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/GoneHorriblyWrong"): The gravity experiments they were conducting involved harnessing the immense power of Arkhium to create machines that could save Fontaine's populace from the prophesied flooding by turning the city into a floating structure similar to Celestia. Instead, they inadvertently blew up one half of the Institute while what's left of the other half is now left suspended in midair, not to mention the threat of radiation fields and other related devices having gone haywire.
*   [How the Mighty Have Fallen](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/HowTheMightyHaveFallen "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/HowTheMightyHaveFallen"): The Institute was once considered a paradise for researchers prior to its destruction. Augustus Lovelace claims that the spirit of research there has been in freefall ever since Raimondo and Choiseul took over the reconstruction project, while Salsa mentions it to currently be suffering from financial problems.

Baptiste and Veronique **(Unmarked Spoilers!)**

Baptiste and Veronique
----------------------

Two individuals intimately connected to the film adaptation of the hit revenge thriller novel _The Two Musketeers_, the centerpiece of the "Roses and Muskets" event—the former, its writer; the latter, a film crew member. As the event progressed, the Traveler, Paimon, and Chevreuse discover that they are siblings and illegitimate children of Morris, financier of the film adaptation, and Elisa, a maid in his household, out to avenge their mother's death at the hands of their father and his household decades ago, going so far as to commit copycat murder partially inspired by that committed by the titular musketeers from the novel.

### Shared Tropes

*   [Best Served Cold](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/BestServedCold "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/BestServedCold"): For twenty years the siblings hatched a plan to avenge their mother's death by lying low and quietly working their way up Fontainian society and stealthily coming after Morris and his associates, most recently the man he hired to kill Elisa.
*   [Bittersweet Ending](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/BittersweetEnding "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/BittersweetEnding"): Both are sentenced to the Fortress of Meropide alongside their father Morris, with Veronique fearing that Chevreuse protecting their father from her killing shot denied them justice for their mother, knowing he will try to buy his way into a [Luxury Prison Suite](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/LuxuryPrisonSuite "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/LuxuryPrisonSuite"). Chevreuse, however, assures her otherwise, and when the Traveler comes to fetch her at the Fortress after personally escorting the three, they catch her convincing Wriothesley to disseminate the truth of their case come subsequent issues of _The Steambird_, so at least they will be given better treatment by staff and inmates alike while at the same time denying Morris such luxuries.
*   [Flower Motifs](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/FlowerMotifs "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/FlowerMotifs"): They are associated with the Rainbow Rose, both due to it being their mother's favorite flower, as well as having left behind one next to the corpse of their mother's assassin after Veronique murdered him. In the context of the novel (and its film adaptation), its protagonists leave behind such flowers on their victims' corpses as a calling card and as a form of psychological warfare against heir father.
*   [Hates Their Parent](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/HatesTheirParent "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/HatesTheirParent"): Both hate their father Morris for assassinating their mother Elisa.
*   [Heroic Bastard](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/HeroicBastard "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/HeroicBastard"): Baptiste and Veronique were born out of wedlock between a wealthy man and a maid at his parents' estate, and Chevreuse mentions that they will soon be treated like heroes for getting their father to pay for his crimes in the Fortress of Meropide once _The Steambird_ publishes the truth of their mother's death and their reasons for revenge.
*   [Siblings in Crime](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/SiblingsInCrime "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/SiblingsInCrime"): Regardless of whether they had been working together from the beginning, Baptiste lied to Chevreuse in order to divert attention away from his sister's plan to commit [patricide](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/Patricide "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/Patricide"), and both of them were eventually arrested—Veronique, for murder; Baptist, for being an accomplice.
*   [Sibling Yin-Yang](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/SiblingYinYang "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/SiblingYinYang"): Baptiste, the older brother, is a recluse, living alone on a house along the southern slopes of Mount Automnequi; meanwhile, Veronique, the younger sister, worked among the people of the Court of Fontaine.
*   [Strong Family Resemblance](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/StrongFamilyResemblance "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/StrongFamilyResemblance"): Both siblings have the same shade of light brown hair. One of them might have inherited their mother's eye colour as well.
*   [You Killed My Mother](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/YouKilledMyMother "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/YouKilledMyMother"): The siblings blame their father and his household for their mother's death.

*   [Big Brother Instinct](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/BigBrotherInstinct "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/BigBrotherInstinct"): Baptiste, being the older of the two siblings, tries to protect Veronique from any interference to her plan to kill their father by taking the blame for the previous murder.
*   [Broken Pedestal](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/BrokenPedestal "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/BrokenPedestal"): Chevreuse was a fangirl of his work. Like him, Baptiste took the heat for his partner (his sister, in his case) for the murder case. All 4 of them end up being exposed and sentenced to the Fortress of Meropide in the end.
*   [My God, What Have I Done?](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/MyGodWhatHaveIDone "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/MyGodWhatHaveIDone"): [Subverted](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/SubvertedTrope "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/SubvertedTrope"). *   [Write What You Know](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/WriteWhatYouKnow "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/WriteWhatYouKnow"): [In-Universe](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/InUniverse "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/InUniverse"), the story for his book is an embellished account for his past; like the main characters of the story, he and his sister are illegitimate children between a wealthy man and his maid, and their mother was later murdered by an assassin sent by their father.

### Tropes exclusive to Veronique

*   [Copycat Killer](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/CopycatKiller "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/CopycatKiller"): Taking cues from the fictional musketeers' method of revenge, she murdered their mother's assassin by sniping at him and leaving behind a Rainbow Rose.
*   [Dramatic Irony](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/DramaticIrony "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/DramaticIrony"): Part of the reason she continues with the plan to kill Morris is because she believes that he would live like a king in the Fortress of Meriopide. Any player acquainted with Wriothesley will know that there is no way the Duke will allow this, but she had no way of knowing due to her lack of connections to him or any of his acquaintances.
*   [Patricide](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/Patricide "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/Patricide"): Was almost successful in giving Morris a shot in the face if it wasn't for Chevreuse blocking her bullet with her musket.
*   [Revenge Before Reason](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/RevengeBeforeReason "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/RevengeBeforeReason"): She wanted nothing more than to get vengeance against Morris for killing their mother via assasin, and in spite of Chevreuse's assurance that Morris would not be given luxury in the Fortress, Veronique still believes justice hasn't been served. It's [justified](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/JustifiedTrope "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/JustifiedTrope") however, since for twenty long years the siblings, being vulnerable and illegitimate unwanted children of a rich and influential man, had no way of getting justice for their mother's death, and had to lie about their background when they were sent to an orphanage.
*   [Sympathetic Murderer](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/SympatheticMurderer "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/SympatheticMurderer"): However morally questionable her actions are, Chevreuse feels some sympathy for her and her brother's plight and desperation, such that she eventually interceded on her and Baptiste's behalf to Wriothesley to at least give them better treatment.
*   [What the Hell, Hero?](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/WhatTheHellHero "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/WhatTheHellHero"): Veronique angrily calls out Chevreuse for deflecting her killing shot meant for Morris, knowing that even if he is imprisoned, he will just try to bribe his way into a more comfortable confinement despite Chevreuse's assurances otherwise.

Berrypuff

Berrypuff / Berrypuffier
------------------------

A Blubberbeast pup originally cared for in an underwater observatory station by an engineer from the Fontaine Research Institute after an encounter with an out-of-control Underwater Survey Mek left it too weak to survive on its own, only to eventually be abandoned by said engineer due to the whims of the Institute and left to starve. Upon learning of this, the Traveler and Paimon decide to nurse Berrypuff back to health themselves.

* * *

*   [Big Eater](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/BigEater "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/BigEater"): Eats several helpings of fish offered by the Traveler while being nursed back to health. Justified, as it had been abandoned in its habitat for some time with dwindling food supplies.

Eude and Blaise **(Unmarked Spoilers for Emilie's Story Quest!)**

Eude and Blaise / Sylvain and Lucian
------------------------------------

A pair of brothers and perfume merchants who come to Sumeru upon hearing rumours of "Auguste" resurfacing, which they question Edgar on. In reality, they are Sylvain and Lucien, two of the four figures behind "Auguste", to which they served as its marketers, and the resulting "Perfume Mania" that hit Fontaine twenty years prior. Imprisoned for their role in the escalating incident, they recently finished serving their sentence at the Fortress of Meropide and came to Sumeru to claim their cut of the profits that they were denied.

* * *

*   [Big Guy Fatality Syndrome](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/BigGuyFatalitySyndrome "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/BigGuyFatalitySyndrome"): Lucian is a large muscular individual, and the first onscreen victim of Kirya's revenge.
*   [Big Little Brother](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/BigLittleBrother "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/BigLittleBrother"): Lucian is taller and more muscular than his older brother.
*   [Disproportionate Retribution](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/DisproportionateRetribution "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/DisproportionateRetribution"): [Discussed](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/Discussed "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/Discussed"). Sylvain doesn't dispute that Kirya has good reason to want him dead, as his marketing did get the police on their doorstep, and he and Edgar did consider cutting Yelena loose on account of her increasing sickness from using her Delusion. However, he angrily questions if [killing Lucian was really necessary](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/MisplacedRetribution "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/MisplacedRetribution"), as his role in the "Perfume Mania", and Yelena's resulting suicide when the authorities caught up, was simply [following Sylvain's orders](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/DumbMuscle "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/DumbMuscle") while he was the one doing all the scheming. No one can really give him a good answer, with the most Emilie can offer being that such a thing is for the courts to decide.
*   [Dumb Muscle](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/DumbMuscle "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/DumbMuscle"): Lucian can come off as this compared to Sylvain. Not only does he have a quicker temper, but he's not quite used to his false alias, requiring Sylvain to repeat himself to get his attention, and his quickness to respond to his actual name when called such by Emilie is what ultimately exposes the brothers. Sylvain even says that Lucian's role the "Auguste" team was following his brother's orders.
*   [Even Evil Has Loved Ones](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/EvenEvilHasLovedOnes "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/EvenEvilHasLovedOnes"): The two marketed Auguste, which they knew could be dangerous to people with high affinity to the elements, and their increasing hyping up of it and the role in the reselling got the both of them thrown in the Fortress of Meropide for escalating the "Perfume Mania". However, when Lucian becomes the first victim of Kirya's revenge, Sylvain is quite clearly distraught, and agrees to Edgar's plan to use themselves as bait to draw out Kirya [for a chance to get revenge for his brother's death.](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/RevengeBeforeReason "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/RevengeBeforeReason")
*   [Faking the Dead](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/FakingTheDead "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/FakingTheDead"): When Sylvain becomes victim of Kirya's assassination attempt, Emilie manages to save him in the nick of time. In order to goad Kirya into believing that he's completed his revenge, Emilie orders the fake news of Sylvain being killed. This allows her to catch Kirya in her trap, and it also minimizes the number of victims, since the knowledge of Sylvain being alive would have led to Kirya taking more drastic measures with his poisoning that could have escalated into a much bigger tradegy.
*   [Laser-Guided Karma](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/LaserGuidedKarma "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/LaserGuidedKarma"): When marketing "Auguste", the two intentionally hid the fact that it can potentially be fatal to anyone with high elemental affinity. Kirya manages to kill Lucian and almost does the same to Sylvain by placing an incense containing Spirit Borneol in their rooms to increase their elemental affinity, and then dabbing "Auguste" on the petals of the Glaze Lily's in their rooms so they'd bloom at night and kill them in their sleep.
*   [Revenge by Proxy](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/RevengeByProxy "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/RevengeByProxy"): It's speculated that the reason for Kirya killing Lucian first and sparing Sylvain for another day [instead of killing the both of them the same night](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/WhyDontYouJustShootHim "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/WhyDontYouJustShootHim"), was to force Sylvain through the pain of losing their sibling like Kirya did when Yelena committed suicide. Although downplayed, since there's also a pragmatic reason: learning the truth about Yelena's death from Sylvain himself.
*   [Shorter Means Smarter](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ShorterMeansSmarter "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ShorterMeansSmarter"): While Sylvain does have the size of a regular adult man, he's not as tall or muscular as his younger brother. But Sylvain is the brains, and he tells his dumber younger brother what to do.
*   [Snake Oil Salesman](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/SnakeOilSalesman "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/SnakeOilSalesman"): Their role in "Auguste" was marketing the perfume to the populace, intentionally hiding the high risk it poses to those with high elemental affinities due to its flower of origin being cultivated with the use of a Delusion.

Montluson (**Unmarked Spoilers for Citlali's Tribal Chronicle!**)

Montluson
---------

A publisher who comes to Natlan to research the country's history for his next book, and requests the Traveler and Citlali's help with confirming some past events, namely the "Battle of Seven Colors". He's later revealed to actually be the owner of a printing company, seeking to find and destroy a long-lost dye related to the battle so he can have free reign to make money off a similarly colored ink he developed.

And to top it all off, Huitzilin reveals to Citlali that _she_ hadn't even been the one to create the color either, having discovered it studying far older materials while developing her technique.
*   [Anything but That!](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/AnythingButThat "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/AnythingButThat"): He's forced to hallucinate his worst fears when he's caught - namely, his fear of going bankrupt.
*   [Arc Villain](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ArcVillain "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ArcVillain"): He’s the main antagonist of Act III of the Masters of the Night-Wind Tribal Chronicles.

Something that Fontaine can't compete with.
*   [Bitch in Sheep's Clothing](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/BitchInSheepsClothing "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/BitchInSheepsClothing"): At first, Montluson can come off as earnest about wanting to spread Natlan's history to the rest of Teyvet, at worst coming off as insensitive to Natlanese culture and customs. Given the fact he was selling a product of a potentially equal quality to a completely different nation, sidestepping the issue could have been as simple as rebranding his ink as "rediscovered" or "now easily accessible" instead of staking everything on its originality. But he didn't, and set up his own downfall in the process.

*   [Evil Is Petty](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/EvilIsPetty "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/EvilIsPetty"): When it comes down to it, his entire plot came about because he was outraged that he was being accused of false advertising over _ink_. Xavier

Xavier
------

One of thirteen Fontainian engineers hired by the Tenryou Commission to build the Mikage Furnace at Tatarasuna, and the only one left following the ratification of the Sakoku Decree. When not working to repair the Furnace, he indulges in his passion for filmmaking. He is the primary quest-giver of the _Tatara Tales_ and _Film Notes_ World Quests as well as being a major NPC in the _Roses and Muskets_ event.

* * *

*   [Brains and Brawn](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/BrainsAndBrawn "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/BrainsAndBrawn"): Forms this duo with the Traveler during the _Tatara Tales_ quest. The Traveler handles all the dangerous fieldwork, while Xavier contributes seven real-life days worth of engineering, analysis, and planning work figuring out how to fix the furnace.

Post-Remurian
-------------

Elynas

Elynas
------

The long deceased "father" of the Melusines, a great and terrible Abyssal beast that attacked Fontaine five hundred years ago whose corpse now dominates the Beryl Region. Elynas's spirit remains intact within its deceased body, and it has become much more benevolent in the centuries since its death.

* * *

*   [Ambiguously Related](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/AmbiguouslyRelated "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/AmbiguouslyRelated"): To Durin, the dragon-like Abyssal monster that terrorized Mondstadt during the Cataclysm at the same time that Elynas was felled in Fontaine. Elynas' crystallized blood is noted to be similar to the scarlet quartz that dots Dragonspine following Durin's death. Moreover, just like how Elynas' heart is merely petrified and can be restarted at any time with the right impetus, Durin's own heart is implied to still be alive. Just as Durin is known to be a creation of the Khaenri'ahn alchemist Gold and was thankful to her for giving it life, Elynas tells the Traveler that it was similarly given form by "Mother", and had many older and younger "siblings" who all adored her for the same. Finally, neither of the two understood what they were doing to the people of Teyvat during the Cataclysm. Thibert and Suavegothe **(Unmarked Spoilers for Neuvillette's Story Quest!)**

Thibert and Suavegothe
----------------------

Two members of Fontaine's old aristocracy who were opposed to Neuvillette being Iudex, and conspired to turn Fontanian society against him by stoking hatred of the Melusines by framing Carole for a murder. The plan not only failed when Carole took her own life to prove her innocence, but then Vautrin proceeded to track down the hardliners and kill them all out of vengeance in an act of vigilantism and sacrificed his reputation and freedom to ensure Neuvillette's place as the Chief Justice would be uncontested.

* * *

*   [All for Nothing](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/AllForNothing "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/AllForNothing"): Their plot to ostracize Neuvillette and the Melusines ended up with the hardliners getting killed by Vautrin in an act of vigilantism and both his and Carole's sacrifices actively solidifying the Iudex's reputation as an impartial judge and the Melusines as misunderstood innocent creatures. 400 years later, Neuvillette's reputation is utterly unimpeachable, and the Melusines are respected and adored by the people of Fontaine, to the point where people actively band together to keep the Melusines safe when word gets out that someone is targeting them.
*   [Asshole Victim](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/AssholeVictim "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/AssholeVictim"): Nobody was on their side when Vautrin slaughtered them, to the point where the audience at Vautrin's trial actually had no issues with him being found not guilty despite blatantly committing murder.
*   [Did Not See That Coming](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/DidNotSeeThatComing "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/DidNotSeeThatComing"): Carole's suicide throwing a [Spanner in the Works](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/SpannerInTheWorks "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/SpannerInTheWorks") was one thing, but they probably did not expect Vautrin to go on a [Roaring Rampage of Revenge](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/RoaringRampageOfRevenge "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/RoaringRampageOfRevenge") and slaughter the hardliners personally in an act of vigilantism.
*   [Fantastic Racism](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/FantasticRacism "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/FantasticRacism"): All too eager to stoke the flames of hate against the Melusines. It backfires on them, however.
*   [Killed Offscreen](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/KilledOffscreen "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/KilledOffscreen"): After they figure out their plan and start executing it, they rather notably aren't seen again once Vautrin decides to kill all of the hardliners out of vengeance.
*   [Laser-Guided Karma](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/LaserGuidedKarma "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/LaserGuidedKarma"): The pair concoct a plot to murder an innocent person and frame poor Carole. They probably would've been arrested anyway, but they picked the wrong Melusine to frame - Vautrin decided that the only punishment they deserved was death, and proceeded to act accordingly. Even during Vautrin's trial, Neuvillette admits that what he did could be seen as a valid form of justice, even if it still violated the law.
*   [Posthumous Character](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/PosthumousCharacter "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/PosthumousCharacter"): They and the other hardliners lived 400 years ago and are now long dead.

Clockwork Meka
--------------

A series of mechanical constructs built in Fontaine. While typically serving as a large percentage of the nation's military might and labor force, they are also faced in the wild as recurring enemies.

*   [Counter-Attack](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/CounterAttack "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/CounterAttack"): The Suppression Specialist Meks in the Operation Downpour Simulation Event: Tabletop Wargame event will only be able to attack melee units if hit first, retaliating with a blast of physical damage.
*   [Crippling Overspecialization](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/CripplingOverspecialization "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/CripplingOverspecialization"): Deepwater Assault Meks were originally designed for taking on larger and fiercer opponents after the invasion of a massive monster long ago inspired their creation. However, in addition to being more expensive to build, they struggle against smaller foes due to being unable to use their full power against them.
*   [Elite Mooks](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/EliteMooks "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/EliteMooks"): Downplayed. They are technically counted as Common Enemies, however, the Specialist Meks boasts more HP compared to the weaker Common Meks, employ more dangerous and damaging attacks, and require two hits from an opposing Ousia/Pneuma alignment to overload their Arkhe energy as opposed to one.
*   [Emergency Weapon](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/EmergencyWeapon "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/EmergencyWeapon"): Whenever a meka loses their Arkhe energy, they will switch to dual-mode weapons that only inflict physical damage, until they recover their energy.
*   [Grenade Launcher](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/GrenadeLauncher "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/GrenadeLauncher"): A Pneuma-aligned Suppression Specialist Mek will be equipped with a Dendro-infused grenade launchers, which they can fire either once, or three times. If their Ousia-aligned variant is completely overloaded, they will deploy this weapon that only deals physical damage.
*   [Jousting Lance](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/JoustingLance "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/JoustingLance"): A Pneuma-aligned Annihilation Specialist Mek will employ an Electro-infused lance to stab their opponents. They discard these in favor of their fencing sword-arm if their Arkhe is overloaded completely.
*   [Lawman Baton](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/LawmanBaton "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/LawmanBaton"): A Pneuma-aligned Assault Specialist Meks will employ a baton to whack their enemies with. If an Ousia-aligned variant loses its energy, they will activate their batons in conjunction with their shield.
*   [Macross Missile Massacre](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/MacrossMissileMassacre "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/MacrossMissileMassacre"): One of the Ousia-aligned Suppression Specialist Mek's attacks is to launch a barrage of Pyro-infused missiles from their Gatling arm.
*   [Male Might, Female Finesse](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/MaleMightFemaleFinesse "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/MaleMightFemaleFinesse"): Most noticeable with the female and male type meks. Annihilation Specialist Meks (female) fight with grace and form, while the Assault Specialist Meks (male) employ their full strength when fighting their opponents.
*   [More Dakka](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/MoreDakka "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/MoreDakka"):
    *   An Ousia-aligned Suppression Specialist Mek will fire their [arm-mounted Gatling guns](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/GatlingGood "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/GatlingGood") and saturate their foes with concentrated Pyro-infused bullets.
    *   An Ousia-aligned Construction Specialist Mek can fire a barrage of Cryo-infused bullets from their left crane-arm, requiring constant evasion to avoid being hit.
*   [Non-Elemental](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/NonElemental "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/NonElemental"): An Ousia-aligned Deepwater Assault Mek can fire dual torpedoes that deal physical damage (a trait shared with their smaller cousins).
*   [Shield Bash](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ShieldBash "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ShieldBash"): An Ousia-aligned Assault Specialist Mek use a shield to bash their opponents with, though they, strangely enough, don't make use of it to deflect attacks. If a Pneuma-aligned variant completely loses their Arkhe energy, they will switch to their shields in conjunction with their batons.
*   [Short-Range Shotgun](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ShortRangeShotgun "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ShortRangeShotgun"): A non-Arkhe Suppression Specialist Mek will use a semi-auto Gatling arm as a shotgun which can only be fired from a short range.
*   [Swiss-Army Weapon](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/SwissArmyWeapon "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/SwissArmyWeapon"):
    *   The launchers and Gatling guns that the Suppression Specialist Meks use can double as missile launchers, and (if their Arkhe energy is overloaded) a shotgun for the latter, and an energy cannon for the former, making them versatile in any combat situation.
    *   The crane-arms from the Construction Specialist Mek is quite versatile, and can switch between a claw, a sawblade, or, even, a cannon.
*   [Sword and Fist](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/SwordAndFist "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/SwordAndFist"): If an Annihilation Specialist Mek is stripped of their Arkhe energy, they will be forced to fight with a fencing sword-arm in conjunction with their kicks.

Icewind Suite

Coppelia and Coppelius
----------------------

![Image 35: https://static.tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pub/images/screenshot_99_49.png](https://static.tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pub/images/screenshot_99_49.png)

Icewind Suite: Duality

Artificed Dancers developed by the Fontaine Research Institute. Bosseut originally supervised its development before Maillardet took charge after the former's resignation. Maillardet then proceeded to give the Dancers combat abilities, making the pair as capable as fighting as they are at dancing. With this in mind, the Traveler can ask Maillardet to set up a spar with the duo to help further his research, allowing them to partake of a deadly "dance" of their own.  
There are two versions of this challenge, "Dirge of Coppelia" and "Nemesis of Coppelius," each with a different set of abilities and rewards. The challenge can be initiated by talking to Maillardet and choosing either version.

* * *

*   [Battle Tops](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/BattleTops "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/BattleTops"): Coppelia's lower body is a top keeping her upright by constantly spinning independently from her upper half.
*   [Blow You Away](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/BlowYouAway "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/BlowYouAway"): Coppelia possess the Anemo element, and she can inflict Swirl if the opponent is already affected by an element (bar Dendro).
*   [Breaking Old Trends](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/BreakingOldTrends "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/BreakingOldTrends"): They are the first boss that
    *   Drops two different types of Boss Drops, though which one you get is determined by which type of battle you decide to engage in by talking to Maillardet.
    *   Does not become hostile upon approaching them.
*   [Dance Battler](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/DanceBattler "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/DanceBattler"): They mix their combat capabilities with their dance and flair. Courtesy of Maillardet.
*   [Dual Boss](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/DualBoss "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/DualBoss"): In an interesting way, they often fight together and side-by-side, however, they are treated as one single opponent (having one HP bar) rather than two. The type of boss you will fight depends on which of the pair the Traveler would choose to get their Ascension materials.
*   [An Ice Person](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/AnIcePerson "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/AnIcePerson"): Coppelius employ his element of Cryo to inflict cold status.
*   [King Mook](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/KingMook "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/KingMook"): To the Clockwork Mekas, more specifically the Specialist Meks.
*   [Mechanically Unusual Fighter](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/MechanicallyUnusualFighter "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/MechanicallyUnusualFighter"): Pun aside, and more like "Mechanically Unusual Boss", the Icewind Suite is the first boss who does not become instantly hostile when you approach. They'll just mind their own business and continue dancing. The proper way to start the fight is to talk to Maillardet, an NPC overseeing the dancing duo, so he can set up the fight for you.
*   [Super-Powered Robot Meter Maids](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/SuperPoweredRobotMeterMaids "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/SuperPoweredRobotMeterMaids"): The researcher who initially conceived of them, Bossuet, intended for the Icewind Suite to simply be excellent dancers. However, Bosseut's forced resignation meant that his co-worker, Maillardet, took charge of the duo's development and decided to give them combat capabilities just because.
*   [Yellow/Purple Contrast](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/YellowPurpleContrast "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/YellowPurpleContrast"): Coppelia is powered by Ousia, while Coppelius is powered by Pneuma. They both only expose this core when they enter Climax Mode.

Experimental Field Generator

Experimental Field Generator
----------------------------

![Image 36: https://static.tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pub/images/screenshot_100_3.png](https://static.tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pub/images/screenshot_100_3.png)

Prototype Cal. Breguet

A creation of the Fontaine Research Institute that has gone out of control due to an accident, now residing within the former site of the Academic Assembly Hall.

* * *

*   [Death from Above](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/DeathFromAbove "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/DeathFromAbove"): Two of its attacks involve it rising up into the air and firing lasers or bombs.
*   [Dishing Out Dirt](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/DishingOutDirt "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/DishingOutDirt"): It can use its gravity manipulation powers to make rock spikes jut out of the ground to hit you or pick up large pieces of stone debris to launch at you.
*   [Energy Weapon](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/EnergyWeapon "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/EnergyWeapon"): One of its attacks has it firing dual lasers at you.
*   [Flawed Prototype](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/FlawedPrototype "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/FlawedPrototype"): It was the product of the Fontaine Research Institute's desire to turn the Court of Fontaine into a floating structure like Celestia to save the populace from the the prophesized flooding. Sadly, it wound up causing more problems than it solved and suffered from many flaws and impracticalities that led to the Institute's destruction. The Automated Supercomputing Field Generator would rectify most of these problems thanks to it being a more compact and streamlined version.
*   [Gravity Master](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/GravityMaster "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/GravityMaster"): It was designed to "counteract" the effects of gravity, [but failed to meet expectations and eventually led to the accident causing it to go haywire](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/GoneHorriblyWrong "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/GoneHorriblyWrong"). In battle, it can utilize an attack to make everything around it, including the player, weightless.
*   [Macross Missile Massacre](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/MacrossMissileMassacre "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/MacrossMissileMassacre"): One of its attacks has it firing a barrage of homing missiles at you.
*   [Shockwave Stomp](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ShockwaveStomp "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ShockwaveStomp"):
    *   After rising up to launch bombs, it will send itself plummeting down to launch one of these.

*   [Super-Powered Robot Meter Maids](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/SuperPoweredRobotMeterMaids "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/SuperPoweredRobotMeterMaids"): Why exactly Eastinghouse stuffed so much weaponry into a device specifically meant for manipulating gravity is anyone's guess.

Automated Supercomputing Field Generator

Automated Supercomputing Field Generator
----------------------------------------

A Local Legend found in the northeastern part of the Fontaine Research Institute of Kinetic Energy Engineering region.

* * *

*   [Boss in Mook Clothing](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/BossInMookClothing "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/BossInMookClothing"): Outside of battle, it looks like an Arithmetic Enhancer Mek constantly performing its "Restore Pneuma/Ousia" move. However, it can be recognized as it is found alone in the middle of an empty space, and possessing a distinct barrier.
*   [Boss Subtitles](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/BossSubtitles "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/BossSubtitles"): "Verified Type Aur001".
*   [Degraded Boss](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/DegradedBoss "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/DegradedBoss"): A weaker version created by Nacker is fought during the "An Unexpected Plan" World Quest, which possesses significantly lower stats and doesn't regenerate its shields after they're broken.
*   [Elemental Barrier](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ElementalBarrier "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/ElementalBarrier"): It's capable of erecting Geo barriers that can absorb tons of damage.
*   [Gravity Master](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/GravityMaster "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/GravityMaster"): Possesses gravity manipulation powers equal to or possibly even surpassing that of the Experimental Field Generator.
*   [King Mook](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/KingMook "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/KingMook"): It's a Local Legend variant of the Arithmetic Enhancer Mek.
*   [Moveset Clone](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/MovesetClone "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/MovesetClone"): Many of its gravity-manipulating attacks are taken from the Experimental Field Generator, like making the player weightless and creating areas where rocks can rise up to cause damage.
*   [SNK Boss](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/SNKBoss "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/SNKBoss"): Like all the other Local Legends, it possesses massive HP and DEF pools, is ridiculously strong, and is capable of wrecking even the most powerful fighters who underestimate it.
*   [Superior Successor](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/SuperiorSuccessor "/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Main/SuperiorSuccessor"): The Experimental Field Generator, while powerful, had a very large frame in order to fit a core that can induce its powerful artificial gravity for offensive capabilities (hence its name). The Automated Supercomputing Field Generator is meant to fix that problem, giving it a smaller frame and profile but still possessing a powerful enough core to perform like its older cousin, with the added bonus of being protected with a sturdy Geo barrier.

Maintenance Meks

Maintenance Meks
----------------

Also known amongst anglers as "Water Maintenance Fish" or "Iron Fish", they are a series of fish-shaped aquatic meka found in Fontaine's fishing spots and can only be caught using the Flashing Maintenance Mek Bait. ![Image 1: Genshin Impact's Ifa smiles gently.](https://static0.srcdn.com/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/genshin-impact-56-livestream-date-time-characters-banners-story-updates-events-ifa.jpg?&fit=crop&w=1600&h=900)Custom Image by Bruno Yonezawa

Sign in to your ScreenRant account

The [**_Genshin Impact_**](https://screenrant.com/tag/genshin-impact/) 5.6 is approaching as Version 5.5 has already moved into its latter half and continues to advance. Version 5.5 of HoYoverse’s action RPG is currently in the period known as Phase 2, where the first banners of the update have been swapped. **Previously, players could pull for Varesa and Xianyun, whereas now, they have the opportunity to obtain Xilonen and Venti in** **_Genshin Impact_** **5.5**. There are still some pieces of content to go through in the upcoming weeks, but some attention is shifting toward Version 5.6, not only thanks to the leaks, but also the livestream.

The leaks, all of which have come from the Version 5.6 beta tests, have revealed several key pieces of information about the upcoming update, including the character banner structure, gameplay details about the two new confirmed characters, a possible new area to explore, a new Archon Quest, and even two new bosses to face, both of which should drop vital materials for Ascension and Talent-leveling processes. **It seems like there will be a lot to do in Version 5.6**, and most of it should be confirmed during the _Genshin Impact_ 5.6 livestream, which will confirm or indirectly deny the leaks.

Genshin Impact 5.6 Livestream - Date & Time
-------------------------------------------

### The Special Event Should Occur Within A Few Days

    ![Image 3: Genshin Impact's Escoffier wields two ice instruments.](https://static0.srcdn.com/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/genshin-impact-56-leaks-escoffier-skill-problem.jpg?q=49&fit=crop&w=825&dpr=2)Custom Image by Bruno Yonezawa

While the developer has yet to make an official announcement about the date and time of the Version 5.6 livestream, it is possible to deduce when it will happen, thanks to the game’s regular schedule. If there are no delays, updates are added to the game every six weeks, and because Version 5.5 arrived on March 26, **it’s likely that Version 5.6 will be added on May 7**. The respective livestreams tend to occur two weeks before the patch goes live, on that week’s Friday morning.

 ![Image 4: Genshin Impact's Wriothesley looks seriously sideways.](https://static0.srcdn.com/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/genshin-impact-57-leaks-skirk-wriothesley-safe-cryo-dps.jpg?q=49&fit=crop&w=220&h=182&dpr=2)Related

##### [Genshin Impact 5.7 Leaks: Even With Skirk, Wriothesley's Role As A Cryo DPS Is Still Safe Thanks To One Minor Detail](https://screenrant.com/genshin-impact-57-leaks-skirk-wriothesley-safe-cryo/ "Genshin Impact 5.7 Leaks: Even With Skirk, Wriothesley's Role As A Cryo DPS Is Still Safe Thanks To One Minor Detail")

Speculation that Wriothesley’s role as a Cryo DPS would be threatened with Skirk’s release in Genshin Impact 5.7 may have just been quelled.

As such, it’s likely that the **_Genshin Impact_** **5.6 livestream will occur on April 25, at some point in the morning**. It’s important to note that this is speculation based solely on HoYoverse’s regular behavior regarding livestreams for the action RPG, so it is still highly subject to change. The event should be officially confirmed by the developer a few days before it actually happens, with complete information about what day and what time the Version 5.6 livestream will occur. If the livestream doesn’t occur on April 25, it could be a hint that the patch itself has been delayed.

### Escoffier May Be A Cryo Sub-DPS

As was previously mentioned, two new characters have already been confirmed for the game. The confirmation came through drip marketing posts made on the game’s official profiles on social media. The first of the new characters is Escoffier. **HoYoverse has confirmed that Escoffier is a Cryo character from Fontaine**, but hasn’t revealed much more information about her. However, the Version 5.6 beta tests have seen her entire kit leaked. According to [Escoffier’s leaked kit in _Genshin Impact_ 5.6](https://screenrant.com/genshin-impact-56-leaks-escoffier-kit-sub-dps-op-ed/), she will be a 5-star Cryo character who uses a polearm in battle.

 ![Image 5: Genshin Impact's Escoffier smirks while holding an ice knife.](https://static0.srcdn.com/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/genshin-impact-56-leaks-escoffier-materials-pre-farm.jpg?q=49&fit=crop&w=220&h=182&dpr=2)Related

##### [Genshin Impact 5.6 Leaks: You Can Pre-Farm Escoffier's Materials, But There's One Item You Need To Be Wary Of](https://screenrant.com/genshin-impact-56-leaks-escoffier-materials-pre-farm/ "Genshin Impact 5.6 Leaks: You Can Pre-Farm Escoffier's Materials, But There's One Item You Need To Be Wary Of")

All of Escoffier’s Ascension and Talent materials in Genshin Impact 5.6 have leaks and most can be pre-farmed, but one item can be concerning.

According to the leaks, **Escoffier should operate as a Cryo sub-DPS in team comps**. This is because she can allegedly summon a Cooking Mek with her Elemental Skill, which follows the active character and periodically shoots attacks that deal Cryo DMG against enemies even when she is off the field. In addition to that, the leaks say that Escoffier can deal AoE Cryo DMG with her Burst and even heal allies based on her ATK. Furthermore, the leaks about [Escoffier’s Elemental Skill in _Genshin Impact_](https://screenrant.com/genshin-impact-56-leaks-escoffier-skill-problem/) indicate it has a different form, which is used for cooking unique types of food.

What differentiates her Cooking Mek’s combat form and cooking form is tapping and holding the Skill button, according to the leaks, so you’ll likely need to be careful not to hold her Skill while in combat.

The other playable unit confirmed for Version 5.6 is Ifa. The veterinarian from Natlan has already been introduced as an NPC, but will make his debut as a playable character. HoYoverse has already confirmed him as an Anemo character, but **the leaks show that Ifa is a 4-star Anemo character who uses a catalyst in battle**. According to [Ifa’s leaked kit in _Genshin Impact_ 5.6](https://screenrant.com/genshin-impact-56-leaks-ifa-gameplay-kit-healer-op-ed/), he will operate as a healer for team comps. With his Skill, Ifa is said to enter the Nightsoul’s Blessing state and hover with Cacacu’s help.

From this position, he can fire Normal Attacks to deal damage and heal allies. Because of this, **Ifa has been largely compared to Barbara, who can also start healing allies through Normal Attacks after using her Skill**. Additionally, Ifa should have some crowd control value, as his leaked Burst says that he creates a wind current that pulls nearby objects and enemies, aside from dealing damage to them.

 ![Image 6: Genshin Impact's Capitano stands still in front of cracked background.](https://static0.srcdn.com/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/genshin-impact-leaks-capitano-playable-canceled-snezhnaya-op-ed.jpg?q=49&fit=crop&w=220&h=182&dpr=2)Related

##### [Genshin Impact 6.X Leaks Claim Worst Possible Outcome For Capitano, But I'm Not Convinced Just Yet](https://screenrant.com/genshin-impact-leaks-capitano-playable-canceled-snezhnaya-op-ed/ "Genshin Impact 6.X Leaks Claim Worst Possible Outcome For Capitano, But I'm Not Convinced Just Yet")

There have been new leaks about Capitano’s release as a playable character in Genshin Impact, but I don’t believe them just yet, despite the evidence.

According to the [leaked banners for _Genshin Impact_ 5.6](https://screenrant.com/genshin-impact-56-leaks-characters-banners-escoffier-reruns/), Escoffier will debut in Phase 1 banners alongside a rerun for Navia, while Phase 2 banners will feature reruns for Kinich and Raiden Shogun. **The leaked order, specifically when it comes to rerun characters, may be incorrect, so the Version 5.6 livestream should confirm when each of these characters will appear in banners**. Even so, the rumors indicate that these will be the characters to rerun in the same patch as Escoffier’s debut. Ifa’s release is expected to occur in the Phase 1 banners, but that could also change.

Genshin Impact 5.6 Livestream - Leaked Map Updates, Bosses, Quests, Events, & More
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Version 5.6 May Contain New Archon Quests & Bosses

    ![Image 7: Genshin Impact's Klee runs with her arms open, smiling.](https://static0.srcdn.com/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/genshin-impact-56-leaks-mondstadt-characters-appearance-story-klee.jpg?q=49&fit=crop&w=825&dpr=2)Custom Image by Bruno Yonezawa

In addition to the characters, which should take over a large portion of the presentation, the Version 5.6 livestream should also showcase the playable content in the update. **There have been leaks mentioning the addition of a new Archon Quest for players to partake in**, which should connect directly to the rumored [new weekly boss fight in _Genshin Impact_ 5.6](https://screenrant.com/genshin-impact-56-leaks-weekly-boss-cryo-mechanics/). This boss fight is said to be set in Mondstadt, so the quests themselves should also take place there. The livestream will likely tease this, even if it holds back from revealing too much information.

Furthermore, there have also been rumors about a new expansion to the Natlan region – a minor area that may be located to the west of Atocpan, which was added in Version 5.5. **There haven’t been too many leaked details about this new area, other than speculation that it may be an entryway to Mare Jivari in the future**, but the rumors have indicated that there may be a [new world boss in _Genshin Impact_ 5.6](https://screenrant.com/genshin-impact-56-leaks-world-boss-mare-jivari/) that will reside in this new Natlan map area.

Furthermore, **the Version 5.6 livestream should highlight the new events that will help fill the patch with playable content throughout its six weeks**. The details about the events have been somewhat scarce in comparison to leaks about previous updates, but there have been rumors about a [new free event weapon in _Genshin Impact_ 5.6](https://screenrant.com/genshin-impact-56-leaks-free-event-weapon-bow-explainer/), which hints at what will likely be a large flagship event.

 ![Image 8: Genshin Impact's Skirk talks, looking at the viewer.](https://static0.srcdn.com/wordpress/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/genshin-impact-57-leaks-skirk-limited-freeze-cryo-op-ed.jpg?q=49&fit=crop&w=220&h=182&dpr=2)Related

##### [Genshin Impact 5.7 Leaks Show Skirk Is Highly Dependent On The Cryo Meta (& That's Not Good)](https://screenrant.com/genshin-impact-57-leaks-skirk-limited-freeze-cryo-op-ed/ "Genshin Impact 5.7 Leaks Show Skirk Is Highly Dependent On The Cryo Meta (& That's Not Good)")

New details about Skirk’s gameplay kit in Genshin Impcat 5.7 have allegedly leaked, and her abilities may be disappointing because of limitations.

Based solely on the leaks so far, it seems like Version 5.6 will be a rather large patch compared to some of the previous ones. Most of the leaks have been reliable, so it is quite likely that what has been rumored will be confirmed during the Version 5.6 livestream. If true, players won’t have to wait too long before playing through the contents of **_Genshin Impact_** 5.6.
